confidence_notes: I used three web searches. Search 1 found the RBA AUD/USD rate of 0.6720 at 4.00 pm on 18 November 2026. That figure came from a search summary, and I did not open the RBA page myself, so the source_url is the RBA exchange-rates overview page from the results. Searches 2 and 3 found aggregated cost-of-living prices for Cairo (Numbeo Oct-Nov 2026, Wise 2026, Hikersbay 2026) and travel-guide bar price ranges. These figures are the reported current prices, not the July 2026 window you asked for. Restaurant and coffee anchors are fairly reliable because several sources agree: cappuccino about $1.70-1.80, inexpensive meal about $4.3-5, mid-range meal for two about $21-28. The beer anchor is higher than Numbeo's $1.38 pint because restaurants and bars licensed to serve alcohol in Cairo are reported at about EGP 100-180. Cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. They come from guide ranges (cocktails about EGP 150-350, wine glass about EGP 100-250 or more), averaged across non-hotel and hotel venues, and they are well above beer in line with local price patterns. Hotel bars charge noticeably more. All four accommodation anchors are estimates from general knowledge only. I did not search accommodation prices or look at listings. They may be off because of seasonality and possible movement in the Egyptian pound (EGP), so treat them as low-to-medium confidence.
comparable_city_reasoning: No direct comparison was needed for food and drinks because Cairo-specific aggregated data was available. Accommodation follows general patterns for large, low-cost North African and Middle Eastern tourist cities, such as Amman (lower) and Marrakech, adjusted for Cairo's weak currency and the large supply of budget hostels and guesthouses downtown and in Giza.
